instagram.author: amjad_masad
instagram.body:
How to Get 1M Downloads in 6 Months
If you wanted to build an app that could get a million downloads in six months, like what are the five major steps you need? A unique idea. An idea that is not an exact copy of something out there because that thing exists. You need a spin on that idea that's interesting. How do you find ideas? I think that's actually the core skill in the AI age. I think if you want to work on a skill, it's going to be about idea generation because the cost of implementation of those ideas is going down rapidly. It's going to go to zero at some point. Step-by-step process. First one, get a good idea. Get a good idea typically tied to a trend. Second, break that idea down as much as you can into like say a paragraph with a bunch of bullets. Like the app, the looks maxing app should, you know, have a camera with an AI integrated, and it should be able to take a photo of my face on my phone or my laptop, and it should kind of draw, I don't know, I'm just making this up, should draw lines. I like, get specific. Like imagine the user interface and get specific about that. Don't overcomplicate it. Don't like add a bunch of features, you just like what is the core experience, how can you get really quickly to value. Users, consumers these days just don't have a lot of attention span, so they're going to give your app like five minutes. And so figure out what's the user journey to get to like a five minute value aha moment. Once you do that, you got your MVP, go try it on someone.

instagram.author: elena.skripalev
instagram.body:
Nothing groundbreaking but it works. 

1. I pay for it.
Gym membership + workout app subscription. Nothing fancy. Basic plans. Super simple. I want to make my money worth.

Paying for something and not using it is just one more way to trigger self-criticism, and I don’t need more of that. Thx. 

2. I block the time.
Workout “when I have time” will never happen. So I make the time. I block it. It’s not optional. Done.

Also the body likes rhythm. Training at more or less regular hours makes everything feel less random. Recovery is better. Planning is easier. 

3. I have to walk the talk.
I can’t give my kids speeches about discipline, responsibility, and following through while not practicing it myself. That would be a pretty hardcore hypocrisy, and kids notice everything. So thanks to my kids, I had to stop preaching and start modelling. If I say I’m going to do something, I am doing it.
